In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the growth response of rice in the field is highly dependent on the growing environment, and the relative response of yield and yield components to elevated CO2 and/or elevated temperature is dependent on cultivar and season.
the response of tropical rice to CO2 enrichment is positive, but that the response of rice to elevated temperature is negative.
the net effect of increasing CO2 alone is likely to be positive in terms of rice production, while the net effect of increased CO2 and temperature is uncertain.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the combination of elevated CO2 and temperature may not have the same effect on rice growth and yield as either elevated CO2 or temperature alone.
the response of rice to CO2 enrichment is not uniform, but is dependent on the cultivar tested and the environmental conditions in which they are grown.
the combination of increasing temperature with increasing CO2 concentration may result in a reduction in rice yield, and that this reduction may be greater for tropical rice than for temperate rice.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the response of rice to increasing CO2 is not uniform and depends on the cultivar.
the response of rice to elevated CO2 and temperature is dependent on the specific environment in which the plant is grown and the cultivar of rice.

, in the context of climate change and global food security, the potential for rice to respond positively to elevated atmospheric CO2 concentrations may be limited, at least under tropical paddy growing conditions, unless cultivars are selected that can respond positively to elevated temperatures.
